newsitem.title: USA: Mexico raised to overweight in UBS LatAm portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Mexico raised to overweight in UBS LatAm portfolio.

text.p: UBS Securities said Tuesday it had raised its allocation for Mexico to overweight from neutral in its model Latin American stocks portfolio.

Along with the Mexico upgrade, Latin American strategist Lawrence Krohn and Latin American equities head Lucia Skwarek cut both Argentina and Peru to neutral from overweight. Brazil remained overweight.
In a report, they said Mexico was raised because "recent data indicate that consumption is beginning to recover. Real wage growth in some sectors should support domestic demand."
Mexico's weighting went to 30.4 percent from 28.6 percent in the portfolio.

Argentina was reduced despite strong economic growth because the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange, "weighed down by the oil and utility sectors, simply offers too few opportunities to profit from a quintessentially cyclical story."
Argentina's weighting went to 10.3 from 11.3 percent.
Peru's cut to 2.6 from 3.1 percent was "based on the potential ravages of El Nio and of growing popular discontent" with President Alberto Fujimori.
Brazil's allocation was trimmed slightly to 40 from 40.4 percent.
The benchmark weightings are from the International Finance Corp's Investable Latin Indexes.
